category_specific_evidence: Issue #19935: np.isclose(6, 10, rtol=0.5) returns True while jnp.isclose(6, 10, rtol=0.5) returns Array(False, dtype=bool, weak_type=True) because integer (exact) dtypes demand equality rather than closeness.
Casting to float first, jnp.isclose(6, 10., rtol=0.5), returns Array(True, dtype=bool), matching NumPy's expected result.
PR#19936 fix: promote isclose arguments to inexact dtype so np.isclose and jnp.isclose agree on the same inputs.
Commit fix: promotes to inexact dtype unless the dtype is extended; extended dtypes fall back to lax.eq(a, b).
Discussion: jax.numpy.isclose on PRNG key types (jax.random.key(0)) caused downstream failures, motivating the extended-dtype equality fallback.
Test added: assertEqual(np.isclose(6, 10, rtol=0.5), jnp.isclose(6, 10, rtol=0.5)) and jnp.isclose(key, key) is True in testIsClose.
reproduction_risks: The passages give no tolerance values for the expected result beyond rtol=0.5 and default atol; the exact closeness formula is only partially shown (|a-b| <= atol + rtol*|b|).
Behaviour on extended dtypes (PRNG keys) depends on the equality fallback, which is not a closeness check.
The issue's system info lists jax 0.4.24 and numpy 1.26.3, but the passages do not state which version contains the fix.
